text:
Nina: Quick design brain dump: instead of PID smoothing, I sketched a leaky-bucket allocator + a unified fallback risk score that blends latency, error-rate, and semantic-quality deltas. Purpose: limit bursty step changes while allowing crisp quality regressions to surface. Thoughts?

Sam: leaky-bucket = rate-limited increase/decrease of canary pct? how do you handle fast rollbacks?

Nina: Yes. Two leaky buckets: one for ramp-up (slow) and one for ramp-down (faster). Fast rollbacks come from risk_score > threshold which mints an immediate rollback token that bypasses the ramp-up bucket.

Luca: interesting. how do you compute risk_score? want reproducible, debuggable math.

Nina: proposal: risk_score = w_lat*norm(latency_z) + w_err*norm(error_rate_z) + w_qual*max(0, semantic_delta_z). Each term z is a z-score vs rolling baseline. We keep weights configurable per-route.

Mei: semantic_delta_z = drop in BLEU-like sim or rise in hallucination classifier? we need an explainable delta, not blackbox.

Nina: agreed. we use two quality signals: nli_mismatch_rate and classifier_hallucination_rate. semantic_delta_z is the larger of the standardized changes.

ops-bot: [schema-check] rollout_policy+risk_score_schema OK.

Sam: what about bursty noise in latency z-scores? z-scores can spike for cold caches. We still need hysteresis.

Nina: the leaky bucket implements hysteresis. It decays capacity over time so single-shot spikes only move the bucket a little. Also add short-circuit conditions: if classifier_hallucination_rate crosses absolute_limit -> immediate fallback.

Mei: can you show a config sketch?

Nina: pasted example below:

```yaml
rollout:
  strategy: canary
  initial_pct: 2
  buckets:
    ramp_up: {rate_pct_per_min: 5, burst_capacity_pct: 8}
    ramp_down: {rate_pct_per_min: 30, burst_capacity_pct: 50}
  risk_score:
    weights: {latency: 0.4, error_rate: 0.3, quality: 0.3}
    thresholds: {soft: 1.5, hard: 3.0}
  short_circuit:
    quality_abs_limit: {hallucination_rate: 0.2, nli_mismatch: 0.15}
  tokens:
    rollback_token_ttl_seconds: 90
    bypass_token_enabled: true
  telemetry:
    emit: [risk_score, bucket_level, rollback_token_issued, short_circuit_count]
```

Luca: tokens? elaborate on rollback tokens.

Nina: When risk_score > hard threshold we mint a rollback_token tied to tenant+route that instructs routers to immediately route 0% to variant and mark the token in audit logs. Token TTL prevents long-term lockouts. Admins can revoke or extend tokens.

Sam: does router need to fetch token per-request? expensive.

Nina: router caches token per-tenant with ledger that respects token_ttl and syncs with control plane every epoch (10s). We avoid per-request RPCs.

Mei: observability: we must clearly surface which signal triggered token minting and what the bucket levels were. Otherwise it's a black box for support.

Nina: yes: telemetry emits token_reason, contributing_terms (list), pre_bump_bucket, post_bump_bucket. We'll also log the raw z-scores.

oncall: playbook changes: Add an "emergency reclaim" CLI to re-enable variant if token was noise. Also alert when soft threshold breaches for >2 windows.

Sam: experiment plan: shadow mode for 2 weeks. Router runs normal logic but we log the hypothetical bucket decisions + tokens. Compare: fallback_count, median recovery time, customer-impacting errors.

Luca: one more edge: A/B tests where quality signal is subtle — the blended score might mask it if weights are wrong. We should support per-experiment overrides of weights and thresholds.

Nina: done. weights are per-route & per-experiment override-able. We'll also provide a calibrator job that uses historical traces to suggest weights.

ops-bot: [canary-sim] synthetic traces executed: spike pattern A (cache cold), B (sustained latency), C (quality regression). Results: leaky-bucket reduces oscillation by ~62% vs naive step, immediate tokens caught quality regression in <20s. Summary attached to PR. :white_check_mark:

Mei: great. next steps: 1) PR with control-plane schema + router caching plan, 2) dashboards for risk_score and bucket_level, 3) one-week shadow run, 4) update oncall playbook. I'll own dashboards.

Nina: thanks — opening PR now and pinging infra for router cache changes.
